what_its_for: This medicine helps relieve constipation by drawing water into your bowel, which softens your stool and makes it easier to pass. It is used for occasional constipation in adults and children age 17 and older when used without a doctor's supervision, but your doctor may prescribe it for longer use or for younger children.
how_to_take: Mix one dose (one capful) of the powder into 4 to 8 ounces (about half to one full cup) of any beverage you like, such as water, juice, coffee, or tea. Stir until the powder is completely dissolved before drinking. The liquid should be clear with no undissolved powder remaining. You can take it at any time of day, with or without food. Do not use more than one dose per day unless your doctor tells you to.
dosing: The usual adult dose is one capful (17 grams) of powder dissolved in 4 to 8 ounces of liquid, taken once daily. The cap on the bottle can be used as a measuring tool — fill it to the indicated line. Do not use more than directed. For children under 17, only use this medicine if prescribed by a doctor, who will tell you the correct dose for your child's age and weight.
missed_dose: If you forget to take your dose, take it as soon as you remember — unless it is almost time for your next scheduled dose. In that case, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store the powder at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it in a dry place away from heat and moisture — do not store it in the bathroom. Keep the container tightly closed when not in use. Keep all medicines safely out of the reach of children and pets. Do not use the medicine after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Do not use this medicine for more than 7 days in a row without talking to your doctor first. Do not take more than the recommended dose. Avoid using this medicine if you have a sudden change in bowel habits that has lasted more than 2 weeks without speaking to your doctor first. Do not use if you have stomach pain, nausea, or vomiting unless your doctor tells you it is okay. Avoid giving this medicine to children under 17 without a doctor's direction.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek medical attention if you experience: rectal bleeding or blood in your stool, no bowel movement after 7 days of use, sudden or severe stomach pain, nausea or vomiting, a big change in how much you urinate, signs of dehydration such as dizziness, unusual thirst, or decreased urination, or if your constipation keeps coming back. Also tell your doctor if you are taking any other laxatives or medicines, as some medications may interact.
when_it_works: Most people have a bowel movement within 1 to 3 days of starting this medicine. It does not work immediately like some other laxatives. If you do not have a bowel movement after 7 days of use, stop taking the medicine and call your doctor.
special_populations: Pregnant or breastfeeding women should talk to their doctor before using this medicine, although it is generally considered safe during pregnancy. Older adults can usually use this medicine safely but should check with their doctor if they have kidney problems or take other medications. Children under 17 should only use this medicine under a doctor's supervision and with a doctor-recommended dose. People with kidney disease, irritable bowel syndrome, or a history of bowel blockage should talk to their doctor before using this medicine.
